newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on hefty liquidity drain.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on hefty liquidity drain.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 180 basis points at 19.00 percent on Friday due to a glut of paper in the market after Banco de Mexico drained a heavy 5.046 billion pesos in liquidity, dealers said.
"The market was a little skittish at the close. Rates were low while there was a lot of market liquidity this morning," a trader said. "But when the central bank intervened, rates began to climb."
Banco de Mexico drained 5.046 billion pesos through three direct sales of paper and eight repos.
Dealers said a sign of surplus government paper in the market was the narrow spread between government and bank paper.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed at 19.40 percent.
Other dealers said government rates may have fallen because the strong peso led investors to sell paper and buy dollars.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts meanwhile closed 1.8 centavos stronger at 7.8540/7.8570 per dollar.
Rates also came under pressure from demand for cash prior to the weekend, dealers said.
Liquidity of 2.242 billion pesos was due to return to the system on Monday from prior central bank operation.
